items.title: Left duals in the monoidal category of complexes are degreewise left duals with a sign-twisted differential
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter more-algebra.tex (More on Algebra)
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-algebra.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma analyses a left dual (N^bullet, eta, epsilon) of a complex M^bullet in the monoidal category of complexes of R-modules, asserting four things: that M^bullet and N^bullet are bounded; that their terms are finite projective; that writing epsilon and eta as finite sums of degreewise components, each (N^{-n}, eta_n, epsilon_n) is the left dual of M^n in the sense of the one-module statement; and that the differential d_N^n equals -(-1)^n times the map induced by d_M^{-n-1} under the identification of N^n with Hom_R(M^{-n}, R). It also gives the converse construction (source lines 18461-18491). The proof unwinds the two triangle identities of a dual pair: from (1 tensor epsilon) o (eta tensor 1) = id and (epsilon tensor 1) o (1 tensor eta) = id it immediately extracts the degreewise identities (1 tensor epsilon_n) o (eta_n tensor 1) = id_{M^n} and (epsilon_n tensor 1) o (1 tensor eta_n) = id_{N^{-n}}, which proves part (3) (proof lines 18494-18500). Part (2) then follows from the one-module statement, and part (1) from the finiteness of the sum eta = sum eta_n (proof lines 18500-18501). The substantive part is (4): since eta is a map of complexes R -> Tot(M^bullet tensor_R N^bullet), the proof writes down the identity (d_M^{-n-1} tensor 1) o eta_{-n-1} + (-1)^n (1 tensor d_N^{-n}) o eta_{-n} = 0, which is exactly the sign rule for the total complex differential, and unwinding the definitions gives the claimed formula for d_N^n (proof lines 18502-18509). The converse is then obtained by reading the same computation backwards (proof lines 18510-18511). The non-routine content is the sign bookkeeping in the total complex that produces the twisted differential on the dual.
